name: Zhangzhung
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Takeuchi, Tsuguhito; Nagano, Yasuhiko; Ueda, Sumie (2001). Preliminary Analysis of the Old Zhangzhung Language and Manuscripts. In Y. Nagano & R. J. LaPolla (eds), New Research on Zhangzhung and Related Himalayan Languages (Senri Ethnological Reports 19), 45-96. Osaka: National Museum of Ethnology. doi 10.15021/00002142
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number Loeb Music Library.69.80.1.4 (19)); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number MUS.69.80.1.4 (19)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the chapter. Sect. 5.1 gives the syllable canon (C1 C2 R V C3 C4) from the manuscripts; the only suprasegmental remark is p. 51: 'Is the language tonal or atonal? It is no doubt monosyllabic and includes many homophonic syllables; in other words, it is a typologically tone-prone type. Nevertheless, there is no sign to indicate the tonal contrasts.' Sect. 5.2 'Syllable Concatenation or Sandhi Phenomena': 'There is nothing much that can be said about this for the time being.'

sources.citation: Haarh, Erik (1968). The Zhang-zhung language: A grammar and dictionary of the unexplored language of the Tibetan Bonpos (Acta Jutlandica XL:1, Humanistisk Serie 47). Aarhus: Universitetsforlaget.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Only the Rosetta Project sample pages are open (contents; pp. 7-9; 12-13 'The orthography of the Zhang-zhung language' / 'phonetic range of the characters' / 'Finals'; sentence and numeral pages). The table of contents lists no stress/accent section, and pp. 12-13 discuss only letters, prefixes, subscripts and finals; nothing on stress. Full text is HathiTrust search-only (in copyright) and could not be reached by automated download the scripted search.

sources.citation: Martin, Dan (2010). Zhangzhung Dictionary. Revue d'Etudes Tibetaines 18: 5-336.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); the open copy could not be downloaded when a reader tried
sources.note: Largest modern lexicon of Zhangzhung with an introduction; a text-based glossary, so a stress statement is improbable, but it is the fullest modern reference and was not reachable today.
